[Dec 2019]

In the early morning hours of Christmas Eve, several people drive up to the *[Palace of Moncloa](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/7/7b/Palacio_de_la_Moncloa.jpg)*, where the Prime Minister resides. The current Prime Minister, [Mariano Rajoy](http://www.elboletin.com/imagenes/portada/mariano-rajoy-9p.jpg), is inside, along with his Deputy, [Soraya Sáenz de Santamaría](http://www.abc.es/Media/201503/10/soraya-saenz-santamaria03.jpg--478x450.jpg). They wait patiently in the foyer as their guests arrive.

The first is the leader of The Spanish Socialist Worker's Party (PSOE), [Ms. Micaela Navarro](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Micaela_Navarro_2014_%28cropped%29.jpg/800px-Micaela_Navarro_2014_%28cropped%29.jpg). The POSE is the main opposition party to the ruling People's Party (PP), and their bloc was in control up to 2011, when they lost a number of seats to the PP.

Second is [Pablo Iglesias Turrión](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b0/Pablo_Iglesias_Ahora_Madrid_2015_-_05_%28cropped%29.jpg), leader of the Podemos party. Podemos stunned the country in 2015 with a massive number of seats and caused the PP to lose their majority in the lower house of the legislative.

Following that, the smaller parties' leaders of Citizens United - [Albert Rivera](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/668753117178150912/C3GqZIn7.jpg) - and Popular Unity - [Alberto Garzón](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4f/Alberto_Garz%C3%B3n_%28cropped%29.jpg) - arrive shortly after. The five leaders and singular deputy sit together at a table where coffee, fruit, and [Magdelenas](http://f.tqn.com/y/spanishfood/1/W/1/L/-/-/Magdalenas-2010.jpg) sit on the table for everyone. While everyone has some coffee, and a few grab a banana, the Magdalenas remain untouched.

**Micaela**: Is that everyone?

**Soraya**: It's everyone. We can begin now. Mariano?

Mariano Rajoy clears his throat and stood up.

**Mariano**: Thank you all for coming.

**Albert**: I hope this is important. I was in a warm bed in a warm house before driving here.

**Mariano**: I wouldn't call you here if it wasn't. But because the topic is sensitive, this sort of...*quiet* meeting was necessary.

**Pablo**: Well, let's get on with it. What's the matter?

**Mariano**: We need to discuss the future of Spain in the international community. Particularly with the recent developments in Europe. With England leaving the EU and the new formation of this ACES alliance by Austria and others, I believe the time has come to re-evaluate whether we with to continue in the EU or not.

**Micaela**: You are overreacting, like normal, Mariano. You know my stance and the party's are in alignment on this. We are embers of an international community, including the European community. One does not simply leave the EU.

**Albert**: Although I understand your concerns, Mariano, I'm somewhat in agreement with Micaela. There are a great many issues that must be resolved before we can even contemplate leaving.

**Soraya**: No one is saying there wouldn't be a difficult transition, or that changes would have to be made. But it's something we have to consider.

**Pablo**: While England leaving was a blow, it is not a fatal one. Frankly, the nations surrounding Austria in the east are less important the the ones here in the west. The EU could use better policies regarding economics, but otherwise is a net positive to be a part of.

**Micaela**: That is not even considering the after effects of England's leaving. They will have to renegotiate trade agreements, have angered at least some percentage of the populace, must deal with losing free movement agreements; they will have many issues to work out in the future.

**Albert**: At the same time, I'm concerned about Russia's military build-up and recent aggression that was thankfully spotted by the Americans. I am not convinced the EU is an effective body to prevent possible future aggression. While Eastern Europe is a long way from our lands, it is something to consider.

**Pablo**: That's true, too. It's worrisome.

A moment of silence falls over the room.

**Mariano**: What do you have to say, Alberto? You've been awfully quiet.

Alberto Garzon takes a second to compose his thoughts, and then says "I have been contemplating this situation for a few years now. I think this is something we must seriously consider." Micaela glares at her political ally as he finishes.

The Deputy Soraya looks at her and says "You are the only one who has not acknowledged that it is worth at least looking at. Of course we cannot be isolationists and must consider the international community. But there are many ways to affect that. Surely it wouldn't hurt to at least consider that other ways may be better?"

Micaela looks around the room at the others, who are waiting for her reaction. She reluctantly sighs, and nods her head. Collectively, the group feels both relief at having come to some consensus, and unease at what the implications of that are. Mariano Rajoy rises again and says "Let's consider our options, and examine the implications of everything. We should have a plan before addressing it with the people, whatever that plan is. We'll meet back here in a few months. Are we agreed?"

Everyone nods their agreement. The all leave shortly after, the Magdalenas still untouched in the center of the table.
